recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Future editorial work could revisit Appointment lifecycle wording with the broader Appointment tracker family, but FHIR-7669 itself does not require a current source fix.
issue_request: FHIR-7669 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Administration clarification request from the DSTU1 cycle asking the Appointment resource description to make it clearer how to represent an appointment request. The resolution says the Introduction was expanded for the request-response pattern and the Notes status-flow display was enhanced with tables.
initial_application: The 2015 Appointment reconciliation sequence applied the request. Commit 44a2cf49ea3e8e7a80153da5d9f6abe2f380525c, tagged for Tracker# 6166, 7669, 6938, and 5713, added the Appointment request/response prose to the Introduction and began updating status-flow notes. Commit 85e9c099b91eab3ae119c8af3bd0f740581ef247, tagged for Tracker# 6105 and 7669, converted the Appointment notes into clearer status transition tables. Commit 42d02e5ebbf5e0b2d8bdd94463554afaa1502a32, tagged for Tracker# 7669, 6105, and 7988, further refined request workflow text and status-flow tables.
additional_context: Appointment and AppointmentResponse are active in source/fhir.ini. Current source retains the clarified workflow: the basic workflow says a requester creates an Appointment with status proposed and participants needing action, the Boundaries and Relationships section explains the Appointment/AppointmentResponse request-response pattern, and the Notes page has tables for typical, rejection/cancellation, re-negotiation, no-show, and waitlist status flows. Related trackers FHIR-6105 and FHIR-7988 concern the same status-flow table/diagram family, while FHIR-5713, FHIR-6938, and FHIR-6166 supplied adjacent status, optional-date, and participant-type context. Later Appointment edits for recurring appointments and Encounter status notes did not remove the clarification. Community searches found no direct FHIR-7669 discussion or conflicting decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because current build-scope Appointment source already explains how to represent an appointment request using Appointment and AppointmentResponse and already includes the table-based status-flow guidance requested by the issue resolution.
